questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: You must drive carefully where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and homes.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires can:

options.text: Make your car more likely to hydroplane.
Make you need more distance to stop.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving on a gravel or dirt road, you should:
questions.explanation: On gravel or dirt roads, you need more distance to stop and it is easier to skid. Always slow down.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train visible or audible, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you, or a train is near. When in doubt, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911. Report the crash to police if there are injuries, deaths, or property damage over $1,000.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, wait until you can see the entire car in your rearview mirror before moving back into the right lane.
questions.explanation: Do not return to the right lane until you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What is a sign that someone is driving drunk?

options.text: They drive slower than other traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing large vehicles. Avoid driving next to them for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Stay away from the sides of large vehicles. It is safer to either drop back or move ahead.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which situations?

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a red light is on or flashing.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns drivers that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: It starts raining while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive closely behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When it rains heavily, slow down and turn on your headlights. If you cannot see clearly, pull to the side and stop until the rain stops.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If cars are backing up behind you, pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that there is an island, median, or barrier ahead and they must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: Using lap and shoulder belts together increases your chances of surviving a car crash.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hips or upper thighs. The shoulder belt should fit snugly across your chest and shoulder. Worn correctly, seat belts reduce injuries in a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: You cannot pass another car:
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another car on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal places to pass.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but it hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and affects your vision. It also impairs your judgment about speed and distance, reduces caution, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
Drivers always check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keep a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always obey speed limits and drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: After a police officer pulls you over, you should exit your car and walk quickly to the officer's car.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car with both hands on the steering wheel where the officer can see them.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections. A crosswalk exists at any intersection, whether marked or unmarked.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, on blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard, sign, or police officer. Drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between yourself and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make hand gestures.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider.

questions.question: After an accident, what should a driver do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop your vehicle at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Driving too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can make you hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Exit at the next exit and come back to the one you missed.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back to the one you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly ahead, at curves or hills, near intersections, on bridges, at railroad crossings, or in any no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What happens when drivers have consumed alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they take.
They lose control over their body, mind, and vehicle.
They become better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They lose control over their body, mind, and vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has many curves and turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce your speed in wet conditions. Avoid braking or turning suddenly. Keep more distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign without a crosswalk, must you stop before entering the intersection?
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.
Speed up as they try to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Avoid looking at them. Speeding up or blocking their path will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What is important to remember when driving on wet roads?

options.text: The road is most slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your tires to lose grip.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Your wheels can lose grip on wet pavement. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from sliding.
